newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela fuel hike sparks no violence - minister.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela fuel hike sparks no violence - minister.

text.p: An unpopular 27 percent hike in Venezuelan gasoline prices Thursday had provoked no violent protests, Defense Minister Tito Rincon said.
"As you have all seen, everything is completely normal," Rincon told reporters.
Prices rose at midnight Wednesday to an average of 70 bolivars ($0.14) per liter -- still among the cheapest in the world.

The fuel prices issue has been extremely sensitive since hundreds died in 1989 riots following a sharp increase. But a nearly 500 percent hike last year was met with a mostly muted response from Venezuelans accustomed to heavily subsidized prices.

The Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV), Venezuela's largest union, has announced a 12-hour strike for next Wednesday to protest the fuel price rise and delays in promised private sector salary rises.
